accuracy.evidence: Checked against Development Matters 2023 Characteristics of Effective Learning (playing and exploring: willing to 'have a go'; active learning: keep on trying when things are difficult) and the 3-4 year PSED statements on confidence in new situations. The 'ask a grown-up first' set is limited to real hazards named in RoSPA home-safety advice for under-fives (hot cookers and ovens, sharp knives and scissors, roads, unknown dogs); food acceptance advice (many calm, repeated exposures, looking, smelling and touching count) follows the NHS Start for Life fussy-eating guidance.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the documented early fixed-mindset beliefs and adult slips: a mistake means 'I'm bad at it' (oops step refuses 'I am bad at this. I stop.' with 'A mistake does not mean you are bad at it'), 'only big kids can', jumping straight to the hardest part (Jump to top is refused on the frame), all-or-nothing tasting (tapping Tiny bite first says 'One step at a time. First look'), and the overgeneralised 'be brave about everything' (oven, knife and road cannot go in Have a go).

lab_distinct.evidence: The mechanism is graded approach to something new: a hazard sort that separates safe new things from adult-first things, a five-rung climb that refuses multi-rung jumps and requires a breath at the wobbly rung, a five-stage tasting path (look, smell, touch, lick, tiny bite) that only accepts the next stage, and a brave meter filled by have-a-go self-talk. None of it matches flagtry (beanbag misses, bike wobbles, tower rebuild for 5-6s) and the 30% shingle gate passed against every flagship lab.

lab_teaches.evidence: The child discovers by doing: dragging the hot oven to Have a go makes the card shake and explains why, dragging the child up three rungs gets 'Whoa! A big jump is hard', the frame will not move past rung 3 until Breathe is tapped, and each oops only turns into the fixed picture (drip becomes a flower, tower stands again) after 'I'll have another go'. The step text confirms the idea only after the task is done.

predictions.evidence: Three locked predictions with tempting wrong answers: 'Yes, every new thing' is disproved when the oven, knife and road are refused from Have a go; 'Jump right to the top' is disproved when the lab refuses big jumps; 'You are bad at painting' is disproved when another go turns the drip into a flower.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Six rotating questions with twelve tagged messages that name the slip: 'I can't' with no yet, only big kids can, throwing the painting away, never again, eating it all at once, pushing food away unseen, a safe puzzle or song treated as needing a grown-up, one fall means 'bad at it' or 'not for me', rushing the scary slide, and 'never' instead of 'not yet'.

readability.evidence: Kid paragraphs are two-to-eight-word sentences about a new food, a slide, paint and a tower (FK well under the family limit); canvas text is two to five words with large emoji, and every action has a big young-class button. Adult text (FK about 6) uses the exact EYFS terms Characteristics of Effective Learning, playing and exploring, active learning, having a go, keeping on trying and self-efficacy.

no_filler.evidence: Passed the filler patterns and the 12% duplicate gate, including against Persisting When It's Hard and Asking for Help. Each kid paragraph adds one idea (trying anyway, small steps and a breath, oops is learning, hazards need a grown-up); adult paragraphs give the EYFS goals, how confidence grows, common adult mistakes and the lab outline.

mobile.evidence: Checked 360 px Android light and iPhone 13 dark screenshots of all six steps: the sort card and both boxes, the five-rung frame with stars and flag, the oops picture, the five tasting circles with labels and the brave meter all fit with nothing clipped; buttons use the young class (56 px targets) and wrap onto rows. phone_sweep reported 0 findings.

accessibility.evidence: walk.cjs: every task completes with Show me on desktop and iPhone 13, the challenge shows, axe WCAG 2.1 AA is clean in light and dark themes, no console errors. Every drag has a button route (Have a go, Ask first, One step, Breathe, the three answers, the five tasting steps, the six word buttons) and the canvas aria-label announces each result.
